coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 6 units (the domain directory itself plus 15.01, 15.02, 15.05, 15.06, 15.07), 36 .md files — exactly matching the expected 6 units / 36 files. Every file read in full through the 3a implementer simulation, 3b rubric scoring, 3c devil's-advocate pass. Rubric dimensions 4 (Constraint Explicitness), 5 (Success Measurability) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are marked N/A across all six units: budget/timeline/compliance axes, launch metrics and competitor analysis are owned by meta/constraints.md, meta/problem-statement.md and meta/competitive-landscape.md, which the domain explicitly references rather than redefines ('Persona definitions live in meta/personas.md — referenced, never redefined here'). Dimension 2 is scored applicable and ✅ because every index carries a populated Role Matrix and every feature file a Role Lens with per-role specific behaviour. Roughly a dozen further candidate findings were dropped in 3c — notably 'does a contested flag block a listing' (answered by 15.02.04's state table), 'per-item value public on a collection' (the 15.04 row is aggregate-scoped), and ~6 stale [PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening] inline markers in 15.06/15.07 whose items are properly tracked by owner-bearing Open Question rows in the same unit.

findings.claim: 15.09 Gear Discography gives the gear owner a consent-to-display lever over discography links in its Role Lens, while its Decisions, its own edge table and the domain CX file state that a link's visibility is owned entirely by the credit and cannot be narrowed. Both statements are unmarked, and they cannot both hold for an already-public credit.
findings.evidence: 15.09-gear-discography.md:23 Musician Role Lens — "Sees which of their gear appears on which records, and **consents to or declines display** — but cannot assert a link"; :25 Operator — "They consent to display of their room's gear"; :26 Fan — "Sees only what everyone consented to publish — never a hidden link, never a hidden-link count". Against: :117 D-02 — "The link inherits the credit's visibility and never widens it"; :74 edge case — "Owner privacy narrows *their* surface; it cannot retract an already-public credit — the link never widens but also cannot un-widen a fact the session already published"; gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:371 CX-14 — "The collection setting governs the owner's surface; the discography link's visibility is owned by the credit (domain 02). They can disagree, and the credit wins for the public fact."
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an owner-side veto exists on the public gear-discography surface (the passport panel and marketplace listing). One implementer builds a per-link owner consent flag that suppresses display; another builds pure inheritance from the domain-02 credit with no owner lever at all. The Musician's and Operator's declared access level in every Role Matrix is ⚙️ Config, which is vacuous under the second reading.

findings.claim: The domain CX file states twice that standing to file a theft report is unresolved, and points at a question number that does not carry that subject, while both features that own the rule record it as ratified and closed.
findings.evidence: gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:228 CX-08 — "When owner and holder differ, both may file, but standing rules are unresolved (Q-04)."; :239 — "3. **Permission intersection**: Who has standing to file? Unresolved — 15.08 Q-01." Against: 15.08-custody-loans-consignment.md:114 Q-01 — "**RESOLVED (D-64 / DQ-MG-04, ratified 2026-07-21)** — **both**, bounded"; 15.02-.../15.02.01-theft-report-serial-flagging.md:99 Q-01 — "**Resolved by DQ-MG-04 / D-05 (2026-07-21):** the owner **or** a party in a custody state `15.08` already enumerates may file, with filing capacity recorded on the flag." The cited "(Q-04)" resolves to gear-registry-ownership-index.md:137 Q-04, which is the authenticity-assertion question, not a standing question.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer reading the domain cross-cut treats theft-report standing as an undecided permission and defers it; an implementer reading the features implements owner-or-custodian filing with capacity recorded. The dangling (Q-04) pointer gives no way to reconcile them from the CX file alone.

findings.claim: A genuinely open permission item — standing to file a theft report under `stale` or `disputed` custody — is stated only inside a question row marked RESOLVED, so it carries no owner and no deferral target anywhere in the tree.
findings.evidence: 15.08-custody-loans-consignment.md:114 Q-01 — row headline is "**RESOLVED (D-64 / DQ-MG-04, ratified 2026-07-21)**", Deferred To column is "✅ [ideation-index.md](../ideation-index.md) D-64 · [15.02.01](...) Q-01", yet the row's final sentence reads "Standing under `stale` and `disputed` custody remains open." The same residual appears in the edge table at :60 — "Standing under `stale` and `disputed` custody is still open" — and 15.02.01-theft-report-serial-flagging.md:99 Q-01, also marked resolved, does not mention the residual at all. `stale` and `disputed` are both first-class custody states (15.08:75, :76).
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a holder whose custody record has decayed to `stale`, or whose custody is `disputed` between holder and owner, may file a theft flag. Both states are enumerated as real, the answer is declared open, and no owner or downstream stage is assigned to take it.

findings.claim: A consented duplicate merge is specified to produce a new third record, while the same feature forbids any record from having a terminal state or being deleted — leaving the disposition of the two source records unspecified and unsatisfiable as written.
findings.evidence: 15.01.01-gear-record-serial-identity.md:141 — "**Merge strategy on a genuine duplicate** … Records are **never auto-merged**. A merge requires both claim-holders to consent, and produces a new record whose chain contains both source chains as explicit, labelled branches". Against :221 D-10 — "**The record has no terminal state.** \"Destroyed\" is an appended, reversible fact; deletion is not offered". 15.01.05-non-serialized-contested-identity.md:94 D-04 speaks only to the pre-consent state — "two records resolving to one identity key **never auto-merge** — both are retained, both claim-holders are notified, and a merge requires mutual consent".
findings.forcedInvention: What happens to the two source records after a consented merge: tombstone-and-redirect (which invents a terminal state D-10 forbids), silent deletion (explicitly not offered), or leave both live alongside the merged record (which defeats the merge and leaves three records matchable by point-of-sale screening on one composite key).

findings.claim: A ratified decision declares 15.01.05 the canonical author of the identity-confidence value set and forbids 15.01.01 from defining its own, but 15.01.05 contains no enumeration at all — and the only enumeration on disk, in 15.01.01, is self-declared provisional and flagged pending synthesis against a set that does not exist.
findings.evidence: 15.01.05-non-serialized-contested-identity.md:93 D-03 — "**DQ-MG-05:** this file **authors** the canonical identity-confidence value set; `15.01.01` renders it and never defines its own … The values are the six already in use on disk" — yet the file lists no value set, mentioning only "photo-bound, no serial" (:45) and "era-unknown" (:57) in passing. 15.01.01-gear-record-serial-identity.md:87-94 carries the only six-value table, and :96-98 states "15.01.05 owns resolution logic and the authoritative value set; this feature owns the render and the record's behaviour at each level. The vocabulary above is proposed from the render side and is flagged for Step 6 synthesis against 15.01.05's." No owner or pipeline stage is attached to that flag, and no second set exists to synthesise against.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the six rendered values are the ratified enum or a provisional render vocabulary awaiting replacement, and where the authoritative definition lives. The relocation D-03 ratifies was never executed, so the file the tree points at as authoritative is silent.

findings.claim: The provenance chain reduces an event's attestation strength when its attester's account is banned or deleted — a rule that exists nowhere in the feature that owns claim strength, and that contradicts the chain's own decision that it is a view owning no facts.
findings.evidence: 15.01.04-provenance-chain-view.md:57 — "An event's attester was later banned or deleted their account (15.01.02) | The event survives … but its attestation strength drops to reflect that the witness can no longer be reached to re-confirm | … event kept, confidence for that link reduced, never silently removed". Against :91 D-01 — "The chain is a view, not a store. Every fact it shows is owned by the feature that produced it"; 15.01-instrument-identity-provenance-cx.md:99 CX-04 — "Claims own strength; the chain reads it. Read-only, no conflict"; 15.01.02-ownership-claim-verification.md:112 D-03 — "The tier is the maximum of standing confirmed evidence, recomputable downward … \"Confirmed\" means \"confirmed and not withdrawn\"" — under which a ban or account deletion is not a withdrawal and leaves the tier untouched.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a banned or deleted attester demotes the owning claim's tier (Counter-attested → Documented/Asserted) or only alters a per-link render in the chain, and by how much — "strength drops" names no scale and no rule. 15.01.02's tier model, which is exhaustive as written, produces no drop at all.

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX file leaves two items marked unresolved with their only deferral target being a pipeline stage the domain index records as already completed, and no owner assigned.
findings.evidence: 15.01-instrument-identity-provenance-cx.md:79 — "Handshake timeout `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` writes the unconfirmed state"; :120 — "Which record keeps the serial? Unresolved — `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`. This is a genuine product decision, not an implementation detail." Against gear-registry-ownership-index.md:30 — "Step 5 deepening has run". The real tracking has since moved and neither marker points at it: 15.01.03-ownership-transfer-handshake.md:100 Q-01 routes the timeout to `/create-prd-compile` (Owner: User) and 15.01.06-identity-continuity-modification.md:96 Q-01 routes the serial-on-fork call to `/create-prd` (Owner: User, `[OWNER]`). The same file's sibling units demonstrate the correction was applied elsewhere — e.g. 15.06.01:99 "Deferral re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5."
findings.forcedInvention: Nothing in the CX file tells a reader these two items are live owner decisions; the stated target has already executed without resolving them, so the deferral resolves to no stage and no owner.

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX file marks two mechanisms as pending against a completed pipeline stage, when both were subsequently decided in the features it cross-cuts.
findings.evidence: 15.02-stolen-gear-registry-recovery-cx.md:57 — "An insurance payout (15.05.03) transfers ownership to the insurer in most policies — which should *change* the flag rather than clear it … `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`"; :105 — "A flag contested mid-checkout. The purchase and the state change can race. `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`". Against 15.02.01-theft-report-serial-flagging.md:101 Q-03 — "**Resolved (2026-07-23): the flag survives the payout and is never cleared … the claimant identity under the flag is reassigned owner → insurer**"; and 15.02.02-point-of-sale-serial-screening.md:56-57, which specify both mid-checkout races in full — "the purchase-time re-screen is the authoritative gate — it runs at payment commit, inside the same transaction that mints the witnessed transfer (15.01.03)" and "Flag moves **active → contested** mid-checkout | Not a block … checkout pauses on an interstitial requiring explicit re-confirmation".
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer working from the cross-cut treats the payout-title change and the checkout race as unspecified and defers both, against a stage that has already run; the ratified behaviour is two files away with no pointer to it.

findings.claim: The flag state machine makes the `resolved` state's sale-blocking behaviour a function of an outcome vocabulary that is never enumerated anywhere in the tree.
findings.evidence: 15.02.04-false-flag-dispute-lifecycle.md:43 state table — "| `resolved` | Dispute reached a terminal external outcome (terminal) | **Per outcome** | outcome recorded, not adjudicated by platform |", where every other state gives an explicit Yes/No. The transitions that reach it are open-ended: :52-55 — "`contested` → … → `resolved` (external authority settles and a party reports it, or the matter is routed to domain 24 and closed there)" and :92 — "Both parties have genuine claims (band split, gear bought jointly) … | Flag → `resolved` (routed out)". No outcome set is defined here, in 15.02.02 (which renders the state at point of sale), or in the sub-domain CX. Q-01 (:145) defers only "binding those states, their transitions and their guard conditions into a contract" to `/write-be-spec`, treating the state set itself as "locked at Level 1".
findings.forcedInvention: The set of terminal external outcomes and which of them block a listing. A flag routed out to domain 24 after a band split lands in `resolved`; one implementer leaves the listing sellable, another keeps it held — and 15.02.02's screening render has no rule to consult.

findings.claim: 15.05.03's edge table defers three rows to a pipeline stage that has already completed, and the first of them is recorded as settled by that file's own Open Question row.
findings.evidence: 15.05.03-insurance-schedule-claim-pack.md:57 — "Insurance pays out | Title typically passes to the insurer, who is off-platform | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — see 15.02.01 Q-03"; :58 — "Gear recovered after payout | Owner no longer owns it; the insurer does | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`"; :60 — "Pack used to support a fraudulent claim | … `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — see Q-02". Against the same file's :101 Q-01 — "**The ownership/flag half is now settled** — [15.02.01] Q-03, resolved 2026-07-23 … What remains is only how an off-platform insurer is **represented** as that claimant/owner", routed to `/write-be-spec`; and gear-registry-ownership-index.md:30 — "Step 5 deepening has run".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the payout/recovery behaviour in the claim-pack surface is decided or open. The edge rows say open against a dead stage; the question row says settled with a narrow representational residual routed elsewhere.
